name: Propanediol caprylate
lead: Propanediol caprylate is an ester of propanediol and caprylic acid used in cosmetic and personal-care formulas, including anti-dandruff and scalp-care products. For appearance, it is listed as an anti-seborrheic and skin-conditioning ingredient, used so hair and scalp look cleaner and clearer of flakes.[1][2]

Dandruff flakes are described by Wikipedia as white or grayish scales on the scalp, skin and clothes, linked to Malassezia yeast, with antifungal actives such as piroctone olamine, zinc pyrithione, ketoconazole, selenium disulfide and climbazole used in anti-dandruff products.[3] A 2025 BMC Microbiology study used propanediol caprylate as one conventional antifungal comparator, alongside climbazole, piroctone olamine, selenium sulfide and zinc pyrithione, when testing a chitinase and chitosanase combination against Malassezia species.[1]
An ingredient database lists CAS number 102731-54-4 and about 30 products containing it, many sold for dandruff or scalp care.[2]

chain: Acts on the scalp environment linked to Malassezia and flaking
angle.text: Used in anti-dandruff and scalp formulas, it is aimed at the yeast-linked flaking on the scalp. People use such products to keep hair and shoulders free of visible flakes.

paras: It appears in scalp-care formulas as an ester-based alternative or companion to classic dandruff actives, and was included among the standard antifungal agents in a 2025 comparison for dandruff-related Malassezia species.[1] An ingredient database lists its functions as anti-seborrheic and skin conditioning and shows it in dozens of scalp and anti-dandruff products.[2]

Wikipedia describes dandruff as involving Malassezia globosa, which breaks down sebum into oleic acid that irritates the scalp and triggers flaking, and lists zinc pyrithione, piroctone olamine and climbazole as the most common shampoo actives outside the US.[3]

No studies found of propanediol caprylate on its own in people. The 2025 BMC Microbiology paper was laboratory work in which it served as a comparator against Malassezia furfur, restricta and globosa; its clinical part (n=18) tested a chitinase and chitosanase solution, not propanediol caprylate.[1]

timeline.event: BMC Microbiology study uses it as a comparator antifungal against Malassezia species.[1]

refs.title: A novel enzymatic approach for a targeted fungal growth inhibition

card.summary: A cosmetic ester used in anti-dandruff scalp products to act against flake-linked Malassezia yeast.

quick.overview:
Propanediol caprylate is an ingredient in some shampoos and scalp treatments aimed at dandruff. People use these for a flake-free scalp and cleaner-looking hair.

It sits alongside actives like climbazole and zinc pyrithione in comparison studies.
quick.mechanism: It is described as an antifungal agent against Malassezia yeasts on the scalp, which are associated with dandruff [1].
quick.risks: It is a topical cosmetic ingredient. Published safety and efficacy data specific to it are limited; irritation is a general consideration for any scalp product.
